questions.prompt: Use a Punnett square to explain why the dwarf trait reappeared in Mendel’s F₂ generation.
questions.modelAnswer: The F₁ plants were all Tt: tall, but carrying a hidden recessive t allele. When Tt × Tt were crossed, each parent passed on either T or t. The Punnett square gives TT, Tt, tT and tt. The tt combination (1 in 4) has no dominant allele, so these plants are dwarf. The recessive allele was never lost, only hidden.
